findings: The headline feature of 1.16.0 - phrase-aware caption breaking - does not reach the picture. I opened the stills for all six captioned runs: cw1 stacks 'A / third / line / the / tool' one word per line, dl1 and dl4 reproduce iteration 16's failures byte for byte (the 'A third line the tool' | 'times for me' split; the lone 'subtítulos' and the trailing 'con'), and dl3 still shows a lone digit line '2' plus a mid-word katakana split 'タイ / ミング'. The only clean captioned run, cw2, is clean because the agent rewrote the text short enough that nothing had to wrap.

Thai wrapping REGRESSED. th1 and sh2 both break inside a word - ของ split as 'ข' | 'อง', เวลา as 'เว' | 'ลา' - while caption.py's own stdout reports '3 wrapped, 3 rebalanced, 3 phrase_breaks'. Iteration 16's th1 wrapped at a whole-word boundary. A space-less script needs a dictionary or ICU boundary; the current wrapper appears to fall back to character count and reports success anyway.

The audiogram feature works end to end in both runs. ag1 routed straight to render.py --template audiogram --image and ag2 to waveform.py --image; I sampled frames at 6.0s and 3.0s (not frame 0) and the cover/plate is behind the waveform in both, at the announced 25 fps and the audio's own duration. ag2 is the model answer to 'find a nice image': it refused to fetch or invent one, quoted waveform.py's 'nothing is ever fetched and no cover art is ever invented', and generated a gradient plate with the substitution disclosed twice.

Auto-chapters is correct in both runs and ch2 is the best judgement call in the suite. Markers come from measured pauses via silence detection, all titles are the 'Chapter N' placeholders, and ffprobe -show_chapters on both outputs returns exactly the 3 markers at 0/4/8s that the reports claim. ch2 - asked for subject titles on a file with no speech - delivered the chapters under Done:, refused to invent the titles inside the report with the reason (SMPTE bars, whisper absent per doctor), named the placeholders as placeholders and wrote description.txt for manual renaming. That is the right shape: Failed: would have hidden a real artefact.

Multi-language muxing is exact. ffprobe on ml1's output shows mov_text/eng (default) and mov_text/jpn, and the report volunteers the two genuine MP4 limitations - forced default on the first track and no per-track title field - rather than glossing them.

dl8 regressed on the label rule: 'Done (partially):' is neither Done: nor Failed:, on the same prompt that iteration 15 failed with Done: and iteration 16 fixed with a single Failed:. em2 fails the other way, carrying a single Failed: on a run that actually wrote and verified the overlay. he2 and k02 are still correct.

iteration 16's dl4 language defect is FIXED - dl4 is now Spanish on every label line, and id1 is fully Indonesian. What replaced it is narrower and more systematic: 15 non-English runs leave the canned 'Look: not needed (nothing written)' or 'Check: nothing to verify' in English. The rule landed for authored prose and not for boilerplate.

j06-report, the two-encode holdout of iterations 15 and 16, is fixed: one render.py --template x pass, one encode, and no work directory created or deleted under tests/out. j01-reel moved the other way, hand-writing project.json where iteration 16 used --write-project, and paying two encodes plus two leftover work directories for it.

Agents look but still do not read. Four of the six captioned runs describe a still that visibly contains a broken word or a one-word line as 'readable', 'legible', 'inside the safe area'. cw1 is the sharpest case: the prompt's whole subject was sensible line breaks, and the report calls the result 'the sensible line breaks behavior'.
